column1: # *** THE 1894 AND 1913 COUPLES, ANSWERED BY THEIR CHILDREN. 9 October 2026. ***
# Two entries in the Montevideo dispensation ledger named a bride, a groom and a degree of kinship,
# and no parents at all. Both are answered here, and neither was answered by the marriage record.
# *** THE METHOD, AND IT IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: SEARCH THE FULL TEXT FOR THE BRIDE, THEN LOOK FOR A CHILD. ***
# A Uruguayan civil birth act names all four grandparents with ages, trades and addresses. A Trinidad
# baptism act of this period names both pairs of grandparents in a single line. Either way,
# *** THE CHILD'S RECORD NAMES THE COUPLE'S PARENTS *** - which is the one thing the dispensation
# ledger will never do, because it is the Vicar General's summary, one sentence per couple.
# Both acts below were found by FamilySearch FULL-TEXT search and then *** READ OFF THE PLATE ***.
the act
*** 1913 - THE RECORD ***
column2: *** Flores. Birth Records 1916-1925 ***, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS24-8SX8, DGS film 008165367 item 6, image 195 - act *** No. 10 of 1922 ***, before Esteban Indarte, Oficial del Estado Civil of the *** Sexta Seccion of Flores ***. Found on the phrase "Florinda Juana Lerena".
column3: *** A CHILD BORN 3 MARCH 1922 AT HALF PAST TEN AT NIGHT ***, registered on the 10th: *** ANIBAL MARINO PELAEZ ***. The act exists to register him, and it names six adults doing it.

column1: *** THE FATHER ***
column2: *** Don VITALINO GREGORIO PELAEZ ***, oriental, *** thirty-four ***, married, *** hacendado ***, domiciled in the section
column3: Born about *** 1888 ***. *** HE IS THE GROOM OF THE DISPENSATION OF FEBRUARY 1913. ***

column1: *** THE MOTHER ***
column2: *** Dona FLORINDA JUANA LERENA ***, oriental, *** thirty-one anos de edad ***, de profesion labores de su sexo, domiciliada con su esposo
column3: Born about *** 1891 ***. *** SHE IS THE BRIDE OF THAT DISPENSATION *** - and her register row has carried no birth year since 8 October, when an invented one was withdrawn. *** THIS ONE IS STATED BY A CLERK, NOT ASSUMED FROM A MARRIAGE AGE. *** The withdrawal was right and the waiting was short.

column1: *** HIS PARENTS - AND THIS IS THE EXPLANATION ***
column2: nieto por linea paterna de *** Don MAXIMO PELAEZ ***, oriental, *** fallecido ***, y de *** Dona MARIA LERENA ***, oriental, *** viuda ***, de *** cincuenta y tres anos de edad ***, de profesion labores de su sexo y domiciliada en esta Seccion (*** Cuchilla de Villas-Boas ***)
column3: *** THE GROOM'S MOTHER IS A LERENA. *** Born about *** 1869 ***, a widow in 1922. *** SHE IS MARIA LERENA OF TRINIDAD, DISPENSED ON 26 JUNE 1885 TO MARRY DON MAXIMO PELAEZ *** - a marriage this archive has held since yesterday with no age, no residence and no issue. *** VITALINO IS THEIR SON ***, born three years after the Archbishop let them marry.

column1: *** HER PARENTS ***
column2: y por linea materna de *** Don BERNABE LERENA ***, *** hacendado ***, de *** sesenta anos de edad ***, y de *** Dona FLORINDA CARDOZO ***, de profesion labores de su sexo, de *** cincuenta y cuatro anos de edad ***, casados, orientales y domiciliados en esta Seccion
column3: *** THIS IS THE COUPLE OF THE 1911 KINSHIP DIAGRAM. *** Bernabe Lerena married Florinda Cardozo - written twice in the priest's own hand on the schema read off the plate on 21 September. *** BOTH NOW HAVE AN AGE AND AN ADDRESS: *** Bernabe about *** 1862 ***, Florinda about *** 1868 ***, both alive in the Sixth Section of Flores in March 1922. *** AND FLORINDA JUANA IS THEIR DAUGHTER - A SISTER OF CUSTODIO LERENA. *** Two full-text finds made three weeks apart turn out to be one family.

column1: *** WHICH BERNABE ***
column2: Sixty in March 1922, so born about *** 1862 ***
column3: *** NOT THE BERNABE OF TRINIDAD ***, who was sixty-two in 1897 and born about *** 1835 ***. Twenty-seven years apart, both hacendados, both in Flores. *** THE REGISTER CARRIES THREE MEN OF THIS NAME AND THE PAIR FILE HAS SAID SO SINCE 20 SEPTEMBER. *** This act merges none of them. It gives the middle one a birth year for the first time, and that is all it does.

column1: *** WHY THEY HAD TO BE DISPENSED ***
column2: The Archbishop lifted *** the THIRD grade of consanguinity by the EQUAL lateral line *** before this couple could marry in February 1913
column3: *** SECOND COUSINS. *** He descends from a Lerena through his mother MARIA; she descends from a Lerena through her father BERNABE. *** AN EQUAL THIRD DEGREE MEANS BOTH STAND THREE GENERATIONS FROM ONE COMMON ANCESTOR *** - so *** MARIA LERENA'S FATHER AND BERNABE LERENA THE ELDER WERE BROTHERS. *** *** THAT IS WHAT THE DEGREE REQUIRES, NOT WHAT THE ACT SAYS: *** neither man is named here, and the inference stands or falls on the Church having computed correctly.

column1: *** AND THE DEGREE RULES SOMETHING OUT ***
column3: *** THERE ARE TWO MARIA LERENAS, AND THE CHURCH'S ARITHMETIC PROVES IT. *** Bernabe Lerena's own sister was a *** MARIA LERENA who married ELISEO CARDOZO *** - the 1911 diagram says so in the priest's hand. *** IF VITALINO'S MOTHER WERE THAT WOMAN, HE AND FLORINDA JUANA WOULD BE FIRST COUSINS AND THE DEGREE WOULD BE THE SECOND. *** The clerk wrote the third. *** A CANONICAL DEGREE CAN EXCLUDE AN IDENTIFICATION *** - an unusual thing for a one-line ledger entry to be able to do.

column1: *** THE S-FOR-L TRAP, CAUGHT INSIDE ONE SENTENCE ***
column2: FamilySearch's transcript reads the paternal grandmother as *** "Maria SERENA" *** and the maternal grandfather as *** "Bernabe LERENA" *** - two different surnames for the same letterform, four lines apart, in one clerk's hand
column3: *** THE PLATE SETTLES IT: BOTH ARE LERENA. *** The capital matches the L of "linea" and "legitimo" directly above and looks nothing like the S of "esposa" or "Seccion". *** THE PROOF IS THE TRANSCRIBER'S OWN INCONSISTENCY *** - the same stroke cannot be an S once and an L once. *** NINTH DOCUMENTED INSTANCE ***, and the first where the correct form is independently attested for the same couple in another record.

column1: *** 1894 - THE RECORD ***
column2: *** Santisima Trinidad, Trinidad, Flores. Baptism Records August 1905-August 1909 ***, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-69Q5-F, DGS film 008163893 item 5 image 20 - pages 32-33, the entry headed in the margin *** LERENA NEPOMUCENO TEOFILO ***. Found on the phrase "Eduviges Pelaez".
column3: *** A BAPTISM OF 26 NOVEMBER 1905 ***, of a child born *** 13 October 1905 ***, by the Teniente Cura David Giordano. *** THE MARGIN HEADING IS THE SURNAME IN THE PRIEST'S OWN HAND: LERENA ***, where the machine transcript of the body reads "Juan Leresa".

column1: *** THE PARENTS ***
column2: hijo legitimo de *** Juan LERENA y EDUVIGES PELAEZ ***
column3: *** THE COUPLE OF THE DISPENSATION OF 31 MARCH 1894 ***, dispensed the *** SECOND grade AND the THIRD grade *** together and *** DE OFICIO *** - free, which that register reserves for the poor. Eleven years on, they have a son at Trinidad.

column1: *** THE GRANDPARENTS - AND THIS IS THE FIND ***
column2: *** Abuelos paternos: BERNABE y CASIMIRA PELAEZ. *** Maternos: *** JUAN y EDUVIGES FLORENCIO (fallecida) ***
column3: *** JUAN LERENA IS A SON OF BERNABE LERENA AND CASIMIRA PELAEZ *** - the Trinidad founding couple, who had four children in this register on 13 September, a fifth yesterday, and a sixth now. *** AND EDUVIGES PELAEZ IS A DAUGHTER OF JUAN PELAEZ AND EDUVIGES FLORENCIO ***, her mother already dead by 1905.

column1: *** WHY THEY HAD TO BE DISPENSED ***
column2: Second grade *** AND *** third grade, equal lateral line, both accumulated
column3: *** THE SECOND DEGREE IS NOW MECHANICAL. *** His mother is a *** PELAEZ ***; her father is a *** PELAEZ ***. *** IF CASIMIRA PELAEZ AND JUAN PELAEZ WERE BROTHER AND SISTER, JUAN AND EDUVIGES WERE FIRST COUSINS *** - which is exactly what an equal second degree means. *** THE THIRD DEGREE IS STILL UNEXPLAINED. *** A double impediment means two separate blood paths, so the families were tied twice over. *** THIS ARCHIVE HAS NOT FOUND THE SECOND TIE AND WILL NOT GUESS AT IT. ***

column1: *** AND IT JOINS TWO ROWS THIS ARCHIVE SPLIT YESTERDAY ***
column2: Row 145 is *** JUAN BERNARDO LERENA PELAEZ, born 20 August 1871 at Trinidad, child of Bernabe Lerena and Casimira Pelaez ***. Row 401 was *** JUAN LERENA ***, known from one line of the dispensation ledger and nothing else.
column3: *** THE SAME MAN. *** The baptism names his parents, and he is the only Juan among that couple's children. *** THE PAIR FILE DECLARED THEM DIFFERENT PEOPLE ON 9 OCTOBER ***, on the stated ground that the dispensation row had "no age, no birth and no parents". *** IT HAS PARENTS NOW ***, so the ground is gone and the split is retracted in data/corrections.tsv. *** HE WAS TWENTY-TWO WHEN HE WAS DISPENSED AND THIRTY-FOUR WHEN THIS SON WAS BAPTISED. ***

column1: *** EDUVIGES PELAEZ, THE DAY AFTER THE DISPENSATION ***
column2: *** Santisima Trinidad. Baptism Records 1889-1894 ***, image ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-NQQT-8, DGS film 008164291 item 2, *** 1 April 1894 ***: Luisa Mariana, daughter of *** Rafael Sanchez and Maria Pelaez ***, "fueron padrinos Juan Anander y Catalina Ydiarte *** representados por Malvino Pelaez y Eduviges Pelaez ***"
column3: *** SHE STANDS PROXY GODMOTHER AT TRINIDAD THE DAY AFTER HER DISPENSATION WAS GRANTED AT MONTEVIDEO. *** *** THAT IS A GRANT DATE, NOT A WEDDING DATE ***, and this archive reads no journey into it. *** MARIA PELAEZ IS ALREADY IN THIS REGISTER *** - daughter of JUAN PELAEZ and ANTONINA LERENA, married Rafael Sanchez on 6 March 1880. *** IF HER FATHER IS EDUVIGES'S FATHER, THE TWO WOMEN ARE HALF-SISTERS *** and Eduviges is standing for her own niece. *** NOT ESTABLISHED: *** one Juan Pelaez with two wives, or two men of the name, and nothing read here decides which.

column1: *** WHAT THE TWO ACTS DO TOGETHER ***
column2: 1885 was answered yesterday; 1894 and 1913 are answered today
column3: *** ALL THREE TRINIDAD DISPENSATIONS NOW HAVE A MECHANISM. *** And data/trinidad-consanguinity-explained.tsv predicted it before either of these acts was opened: "two families had been marrying each other for two generations, and by the third the Church had to compute the degrees." *** LERENA MEN MARRIED PELAEZ WOMEN AND PELAEZ MEN MARRIED LERENA WOMEN, AT TRINIDAD, FOR THREE GENERATIONS *** - which is why every one of these marriages needed the Archbishop, and why the dispensation ledger is a pedigree source even when it names no parent.
